Doctor of Philosophy In Chemical…
Chemical Engineering Ph.D.
A research-intensive Ph.D. program that provides advanced training in chemical engineering, preparing students to tackle complex challenges at the intersection of energy, materials, sustainability, and manufacturing. Students conduct original, high-impact research under close faculty mentorship, with access to cutting-edge facilities and interdisciplinary collaborations across Syracuse University.
Degree Requirements
A minimum of 42 credit hours is required for the completion of the Ph.D. degree, including at least 24 credits in chemical engineering. No credits are given for dissertation research. A student entering the Ph.D. program with a M.S. degree may apply up to 30 credits toward the required coursework, with the approval of the program director. A minimum of three years of graduate study is required and students typically complete all requirements within five years.
Chemical engineering Ph.D. students may be eligible for the interdisciplinary training program funded by the National Science Foundation (NSF). The Emergent Intelligence Graduate Training Program (EMIRGE) at the BioInspired Institute offers fully funded research fellowship opportunities.
View program details in the University Course Catalog.
